title: claude --restricted Removes Bash
caption:
My allow rules were quietly doing more than I thought.

--restricted shipped in Claude Code v2.1.248 on Aug 28. No Bash, no code execution, no WebFetch, file tools pinned to the working directories. And it loads only managed settings plus --settings — your user, project and local files are ignored.

That last part is the whole point, and it's the part I'd have skipped if I'd built it. An allowlist you can edit from inside the repo isn't an allowlist.

Would you run it on a client repo?

slides.headline:
--restricted
removes Bash.
slides.sub: v2.1.248, Aug 28. The built-in tools that run commands or code leave the session. So does WebFetch.

slides.title: what the flag strips
items: Tools that run commands or code, unless you name them in --tools
WebFetch, by the same rule. The default preset doesn't count
Read, Write and Edit confined to the session's working directories
It refuses bypassPermissions, and refuses to create cloud sessions

slides.headline:
Your settings
stop loading.
slides.sub: Only managed settings and --settings apply. Your user, project and local files are ignored.

slides.title: Built for shared machines
slides.sub: The case in the docs: an eval harness that must not run commands or read local settings.
